 JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.8,50,000/- for the death of Smt. Lakshmi in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
Mahandran vs Selvamani.K on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75858227/
2 2.

That on 14-06-2022 at about 8-00 a.m. Smt.Lakshmi along with one Pushpa were walking on Subbaiah Reddy Road, when they reached near Ganga Automobiles Garage, at that time, rider of Hero Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-05/JC-9607 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life, came at high speed and dashed the deceased.
Due to which, deceased fell down and sustained head injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to NIMHANS, Bengaluru, wherein she took first aid treatment as per the doctors' advice she was shifted to Bowring hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she succumbed to the injuries.
The petitioners have spent huge amount towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

3. It is further stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy,
was aged about 66 years and working as a House keeper and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners became dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
4. It is contended that the accident was occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the Hero Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-05/JC-9607.

In this regard, criminal case was registered against her, in Crime No.62/2022 for the offences punishable under sections 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
and Section 134(A & B) R/W Section 187 of IMV Act by the jurisdictional police.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
5. After service of the notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence she have appeared through their respective counsel and filed written statements.
6. The respondent No.2, in the written statement contended that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the deceased and not on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further stated that the offending vehicle having valid insurance policy at the time of accident.
Further denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.
This respondent has contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant and without any basis.
Further contended that at the time of accident offending vehicle had insurance policy, which was in force.
Further contended that medical records indicate that she was admitted to the hospital on 24.6.2022 and died on 14.6.2022.
The said fact clearly indicates that the death is not due to the alleged accident.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. The respondent No.3 has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-05/JC-9607 and the same is valid on the date of accident.
Further contended that, alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased and there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

Further contended that rider of the offending vehicle was minor at the time of accident and in the reply notice, the owner of the vehicle admitted that rider not having any DL at the time of accident, hence the respondent No.3 is not liable to pay the compensation.
Further denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.

Mahandran vs Selvamani.K on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75858227/
3
Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition.

8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that Lakshmi W/o Late. Munishami had died in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 14.6.2022 at about 8.00 a.m. on Subbaih Reddy Road near Ganga Automobiles Garage, Halasoor, Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Hero Honda Active bearing registration No.KA-05-JC-9607 in an actionable negligence?
2.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
3.
What order
or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.2 was examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
10.

On the other hand, to prove the defences of the respondent No.2, has examined Legal Manager of the insurance company as RW1.
11.
Heard arguments of both sides.
At the time of arguments 12.

My findings to the above issues as follows:
Issue No.1: Affirmative. Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3:

As per final order,
for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
13.
It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.KA-05-JC-9607, the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Smt.Lakshmi had died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.

14. On the contrary, the respondent No.2 has contended that, she was parking the vehile infront of her house, so she was not riding the said vehicle, the deceased while walking near the house had stumbled on the road and fell down, the family of the respondent had enquired her and found that she was fine.

Further contended that as per medical records indicate that petitionr was admitted to the hospital on 24.6.2022, after 10 days of the accident and complaint has been lodged on after 10 days of the accident.
The said fact clearly idicates tht the death of Smt.Lakshmi is not due to the alleged accident occurred on 14.6.2022.

Mahandran vs Selvamani.K on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75858227/
4 15.
Apart from this, the respondent No.3 has not disputed the accident and the death of Smt.Lakshi.
But strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
16. In such a situation, burden is more on the part of the petitioners, to prove the above issues on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
17. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 has examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to Ex.P11
. Ex.P1-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.62/2022 of Halasuru Traffic Police Station.
Ex. P2-true copy of first information statement given by Manohar,
Ex. P3- true copy of PM report,
Ex.P4-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex

.P5-true copy of notice, Ex.P6-true copy of inquest report, Ex.P7-true copy of charge sheet, Ex.P8 & Ex.P9-notice u/s 133 of MV Act and its reply, Ex.P10-true copy of IMV report and Ex.P11- true copy of spot sketch.

18. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by Manohar, the S.H.O. of Halasuru Traffic police has registered the case against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of I.P.C and Section 134(A & B) R/W Section 187 of IMV Act.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC and Section 134(A & B) R/W Section 187, 129 R/W 177, 4(1) R/W 181 of IMV Act.
19.
In order to substantiate her case, the respondent No.2 has not stepped into the witness box to prove her contention.

During the course of arguments the counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that the alleged accident occurred on 14.6.2022 and complaint was lodged on 24.6.2022,
after a lapse of 10 days.
Hence, the death of Lashmi is not due to the accidental injuries.
20. On going through the complaint marked at Ex.P2 filed by Manohar, the son of the petitioner on 24.6.2022.
There is delay of 10 days in filing the complaint.

At this stage, on the point of delay, the petitioner has relied the decisions reported in 2010 ACJ 736 between Karan Singh and Anshuman &
Others and (2011) 4 SCC Page 693, between, Ravi V/ S. Badrinarayan, "It was observed that, "delay in lodging F.I.R cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case. Knowing that the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the police station immediately, after the accident.
As the family members give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the police station.

Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the F.I.R with the police."
21.
On going through the complaint there is a clear mention about the reasons for delay in lodging the complaint.
The delay in lodging the FIR is not a ground to doubt the claim petition.
22. Further the respondent No.2 has not placed reliable documents to prove that the deceased while walking had stumbled on the road and fell down due to which she sustained head injury.
On going through the P.M. report marked at Ex.P3 the cause of death mentioned as "Death is due to coma as a result of head injury sustained".

To disprove the said fact, the respondent No.2 has not examined Mahandran vs Selvamani.K on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75858227/
5
either the author of the document or placed any document to show that death is not the due to the accidental injuries.
23. Added to this, the respondent No.3 has examined its Legal Manager as RW1.
But his evidence will not much helpful to disprove the case of the petitioner.

24. Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent No.1 & 3 about the denial of allegation made against the rider of the offending vehicle.
25. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing No.KA-05-JC-9607 and in the said accident, Smt.Lakshmi succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.
ISSUE No.2;
26.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P12 to Ex.P14 Aadhar cards of the petitioners,
have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.
27. In the case on hand, no doubt the major sons and daughter of Smt.Lakshmi filed this claim petition.
According to them, they were dependents to the deceased petitioner during her lifetime.
In the cross-examination PW1 has stated that himself and his brother petitioner No.1 were residing separately and the petitioner No.3 was married and residing in her husband's house.
Here, it is necessary discuss the point that, mother place an important role in the family.
All the children, one or the other way defendants to their parents whether they are minors or majors, married or unmarried.
But the percentage of disability may be varied from one person to another person.
During the minority of the child, dependency is more on the parents.
After the marriage of the children, the percentage of disability is less on the parents, if compare with the minor children.

28. In the case on hand, by looking to the age criteria though they are major sons, they could have dependents to their parents not only economically, but in connection with love and affection during his lifetime.
Hence, the petitioners can be presumed as dependents to their mother during her lifetime in the absence of contra materials from the other side.

In this regard, relied the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court (DB), in National Insurance Company Limited V/S Birender and Others stated that, a major and earning son has a right to claim compensation under Motor Vehicle Act.

In this case, by referring the case of Manjuri Bera, stated that, even if there is no loss of dependency,

6 the claimant if he was a legal representative will be entitled to compensation.

sentences.text:
Even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation, and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application,
irrespective of the fact, whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
29.

The petitioners herein, to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident,
have not placed any document.
On perusal of P.M. report marked at Ex.P3, the age of the deceased was mentioned as 66 years.
The said document remained unquestioned by the other side.
Hence, it is safely to be considered that, as on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged about 66 years.
For her age, multiplier '5' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.

30. In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition, and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was doing house keeping work and used to earn income of Rs.15,000/-
per month.
But in support of definite income of the deceased, there is no iota of documents.
By considering the present life condition and escalation of rates, it is just and proper to consider Rs.15,000/- per month.
31. Another point to be taken in to consideration herein that, as per the petition, 3 persons were depending on the earning of the deceased.
In this regard, about the deduction of the personal and living expenses is concerned, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.
32. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "

33. Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependant family members exceeds six."
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.

In the present case,
Mahandran vs Selvamani.K on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75858227/
7 deceased was aged about 66 years, as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "5" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month.
And Rs.1,80,000/- per year.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus, net loss income comes to Rs.1,20,000/-(Rs.1,80,000-Rs.60,000).This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "5".
Which comes to Rs.6,00,000/-.

34 . Apart from this, aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium, and with respect to the funeral expenses, to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.
National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

35. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 3 under the head loss of consortium.

LIABILITY:
38.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-05-JC-9607 alleged accident had taken place.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

39. The respondent No.3-Insurance Company has contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was a minor, aged about 14 years and had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

The police have filed charge sheet against Kumr.Anbuvarshini u/s 279, 304(A) of IPC &
134(A & B) R/w Section 187, 129, R/W 177, 4 (1) R/W 181 of IMV Act and also filed charge sheet under Section 5 R/W Section 180 of IMV Act against the owner of the vehicle.
Thereby violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
As such, insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
To substantiate the same, respondent No.3 has examined Manager-Legal Claim as RW1.
He has reiterated the contents as averred in the written statement.

In the cross examination suggested that is there any documents to show that the respondent No.2 was a minor at the time of accident, for which he has clearly stated that in the charge sheet and notice clearly mentioned the age of the rider of the offending vehicle.

40. In this regard, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer, relevant provision has been inserted stating that, at the time of accident the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence.

To disprove the contents of the charge sheet and to show that,
the rider had valid D.L. no supportive evidence is available on record to impeach the recitals of Ex.P7. Added to this on perusal of Ex.P9 reply to notice u/s 133 of MV Act clearly mentioned as " at the time of accident rider 2 wheeler by name S.K.Anuvarshni, 14 years, riding two wheeler is not having licence ".
41.
During the course of argument the learned counsel for the respondent No.3 has argued that as on the date of accident the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid licence.
It is violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

Hence, respondent No.3 is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and has relied the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA 7683/2014 in case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Bibi Nafisa & Others 42.

On perusal of the supra decision, the principle laid down in the supra decision is that "where a minor boy under the age of 16 years cannot be said to be a qualified person to apply for driving licence".

9 43.
In the instant case the rider of the offending vehicle was a minor aged about 14 years as stated in reply notice as per Ex.P9.
Hence, it is crystal clear that as on the date of accident rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.3 is the insurance company has absolve from its liability to pay the compensation.
Hence, the decision relied by the respondent No.3 is aptly applicable to the facts of this case on hand.

44. In the light of the discussion held above, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, cannot escape from her liability to pay compensation to the petitioners, in view of violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, respondent No.1 being the owner is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
45.

In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act as against the respondent No.1 & 2 hereby partly allowed with costs.
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act as against the respondent No.3 is hereby dismissed.

The petitioners are entitled for  compensation of Rs.7,65,000/- (Rupees seven lakh sixty five thousand only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 to 3 shall be awarded equally.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 to 3, since the amount is very meagre, entire amount shall be released to them through due process of law.

each.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.8,50,000/- for the death of Smt. Lakshmi in a road traffic accident.
Due to the untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners became dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
4. It is contended that the accident was occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the Hero Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-05/JC-9607.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
This respondent has contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant and without any basis.
But strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
opennyai_summary.issue:

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that Lakshmi W/o Late. Munishami had died in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 14.6.2022 at about 8.00 a.m. on Subbaih Reddy Road near Ganga Automobiles Garage, Halasoor, Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Hero Honda Active bearing registration No.KA-05-JC-9607 in an actionable negligence?
2.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, at what rate and from whom?
3.
What order
or award?
